transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sophie Martinez (Orion Dir of ML), Liam O'Connor (Orion Platform), Raj Patel (Orion Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync focused on model selection and version pinning. Discussed benchmark results from last run, observed p95 latency spike on peak, compared quantized variant tradeoffs, agreed on 1% canary and rollback plan. Next steps: run canary, share pricing, legal to review security pack.

Topics: model selection, version pinning, rollbacks/fallbacks, canary strategy, perf/cost tradeoffs, security/compliance ask

Transcript:
[00:00] Daniel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, gonna kick off, uh, quick agenda — perf results, model selection, pinning and canary plan, legal / security checkpoints. Sophie thanks for coming in.
[00:08] Sophie: yeah thanks, good to be here. quick note, we're about to go into a retail promo spike next week so we wanted to make sure the pinned model doesn't regress on hallucination or latency.
[00:18] Priya: great, thanks. we ran the batch benchmarks overnight with rwx-13b-v1.2.0 and the quantized build rwx-13b-quant-v1.2, also a fallback to rwx-13b-v1.1.7 in case we need to roll back. i'll share the raw logs after — some of the tokens got cut in the transcription but i'll upload the csv.
[00:36] Liam: can you summarize numbers quickly? the spreadsheet had a lot of columns.
[00:40] Priya: sure. p50 for rwx-13b-v1.2.0 on our test mix was ~120ms, p95 around 420ms, error rate about 0.8% on the synthetic queries. quantized gave p50 110ms, p95 490ms, error rate 1.6% so tradeoff is cost vs slight increase in hallucination-ish behavior. cost delta: full fp ~ $0.45 per 1k tokens, quant ~ $0.22 per 1k tokens in our cluster math. note these are approximate.
[01:12] Raj: is that with KV cache warm? because our use is chatty and cache hit rate matters.
[01:16] Priya: good point — the run had prefix caching enabled and hit rate was ~72% based on replay, so numbers reflect a warm-ish cache. cold-starts will see higher p95.
[01:26] Sophie: last week we saw a p95 spike to 1.2s during the afternoon — is that from batching or GPU saturation?
[01:31] Priya: looked like a mixture — the routing policy sent some large seq-length requests to the same worker. memory pressure caused queueing; we tuned batch size to 8 but for long seq it still bumped. we can set a per-route cap and fall back to dedicated nodes or to the older v1.1.7 which uses a different kernel path that's a bit more stable under long sequences.
[01:52] Daniel: so action: pin to v1.2.0 but keep automated fallback to v1.1.7 and a canary of 1% traffic for 48 hours, is that fair?
[01:59] Sophie: sounds good, as long as rollback is fast. we need a playbook: who triggers rollback and how long until full cutover.
[02:05] Priya: we recommend automatic detection on error rate >1.5% or p95 > 700ms for 10 minutes and then an auto-failover to the pinned fallback, with alerting to your oncall. manual rollback can be triggered from Console — takes ~2-3 minutes to shift routing depending on connections.
[02:23] Liam: what's the risk of semantic regression if we switch to the older v1.1.7? our product team worried about answer quality.
[02:28] Priya: v1.1.7 is slightly more conservative, F1 on our prompt set drops ~2.5 points compared to v1.2.0; hallucination frequency lower for certain financial entity extraction cases. so it's tradeoff: latency/stability vs slight drop in correctness.
[02:42] Raj: any concerns about tokenization differences across versions? we've seen weird token breaks.
[02:47] Priya: small differences, yes. v1.2.0 uses updated tokenizer merges for some retail-specific tokens, we flagged two prompts where spacing changed results; we'll include those in the eval harness as regression tests.
[02:59] Daniel: ok on pricing — quick note — if you use quantized variant you cut costs nearly in half but we saw some quality delta, and also quantization can change hallucination profile. i'll send a cost spreadsheet with traffic scenarios.
[03:09] Sophie: would like to see a blended cost for our traffic distribution.
[03:13] Daniel: will do.
[03:15] Sophie: also on compliance side, we need the SOC2 and KMS integration docs, plus a note on data residency for EU customers.
[03:23] Daniel: yes we have the security pack, i'll share the link. we support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated and encrypted-at-rest for hosted.
[03:31] Priya: quick technical note — for the canary we suggest disabling aggressive batching and set max_batch_latency to 10ms to reduce p95 spikes on variable seq lengths. also set KV cache TTL to 30s for the canary to mimic production chatty pattern.
[03:47] Liam: do we need Dedicated for the promo spike or can we rely on hosted with autoscale?
[03:51] Priya: depends on SLA. hosted autoscale can handle burst but there's noisy neighbor risk; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. for short promo spikes hosted with reserved burst is usually fine. if you want strict p95 SLAs I'd recommend Dedicated or a dedicated pool in Redwood Dedicated.
[04:08] Sophie: timeline wise we need the canary before next Monday. today is Wednesday so is that feasible?
[04:12] Priya: yes, we can spin up the canary tomorrow, run 48h and aim to be ready by Sunday evening; we'll need the traffic profile from Liam and the pinned config file from us.
[04:21] Daniel: ok so list of deliverables: Priya runs canary; Daniel sends pricing and security links; Liam shares traffic profile; Sophie coordinates legal.
[04:30] Raj: one more thing — fallback to a smaller model if GPU gets saturated? is that supported?
[04:34] Priya: yes, we support automatic routing by policy to a cheaper model variant — e.g., rwx-7b-quant as fallback for non-critical routes, or to a CPU-safe lower model. routing rules are per-route in Console.
[04:45] Sophie: can you show on the next call how to set the policy and the dashboard alerts?
[04:49] Daniel: sure, we can demo that.
[04:51] Priya: i'll also include a quick runbook for rollback and canary metrics to watch (p50, p95, error rate, hallucination score from eval harness).
[04:59] Sophie: perfect.
[05:00] Daniel: any competitors we should consider as bench? Sophie: we looked briefly at Anthropic and HF, but the main comparison is cost vs latency vs control.
[05:08] Liam: ok yeah.
[05:10] Daniel: last bit — documentation links: pricing spreadsheet (link will be emailed), security pack (link), canary runbook (Priya will upload), eval harness with regression prompts (Priya).
[05:21] Sophie: that covers it for us. thanks everyone.
[05:24] Daniel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the items and set next sync for next Wednesday same time.

References / Links (mentioned): pricing spreadsheet (to be sent), security pack (SOC2/KMS docs), canary runbook, eval harness CSV (regression prompts).

End of transcript.
